query: How does resolution time vary by agent and issue type?

per_column.name: issue_type
per_column.rationale: Directly provides the issue-type axis the query needs. Categorisations (database_access, vpn_connectivity, network_connectivity, software_application) are sound readings of the short_description text.

per_column.name: issue_symptom
per_column.rationale: Adds a second, orthogonal grouping axis (symptom) that complements issue_type for resolution-time analysis. Values like connection_failure, no_access, other are well-warranted from the descriptions.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The agent axis is central to the query, but this largely restates the original assigned_to column, limiting new leverage. Values appear grounded (agent names present in table).

per_column.name: resolver_agent
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes the resolver from the assignee, a genuinely useful distinction for per-agent resolution-time; likely derived from closed_by. Values plausibly grounded, though closed_by mapping not shown in samples.

per_column.name: reassigned
per_column.rationale: A reassignment flag is a meaningful driver of resolution time and a new analytical axis. Derivable by comparing assigned vs resolver, but the sampled derivations (e.g., assigned==resolver yet marked reassigned in some rows) raise mild consistency concerns.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply the two grouping axes the query needs (issue type/symptom and agent), plus a reassignment flag that enriches resolution-time analysis. assigned_agent overlaps heavily with the existing assigned_to column, reducing its added value. Values are well grounded in the source text, with only minor concerns about the derivation logic for reassigned/resolver where the mapping is not fully visible in the samples.
